Closes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/8968

```
$ promtool check sd config.yml http_example 20s
Target: localhost:9090
Original Labels:
	__address__ = "localhost:9090"
	__meta_url = "http://localhost:8090/hello"
	foo_1 = "bar_1"
	foo_2 = "bar_2"
After relabeling:
	__address__ = "localhost:9090"
	__meta_url = "http://localhost:8090/hello"
	foo_1 = "bar_1"
	foo_2 = "bar_2"
	t_1 = "bar_1"

Target: localhost:9090
Original Labels:
	__address__ = "localhost:9090"
	__meta_url = "http://localhost:8090/hello"
	foo_1 = "bar_1"
	foo_2 = "bar_2"
After relabeling:
	__address__ = "localhost:9090"
	__meta_url = "http://localhost:8090/hello"
	foo_1 = "bar_1"
	foo_2 = "bar_2"
	t_1 = "bar_1"


$ cat config.yml
...
  - job_name: 'http_example'
    relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [foo_1]
      target_label: t_1
    http_sd_configs:
      - url: http://localhost:8090/hello
        refresh_interval: 50s
...
```

issue_context.title: Promtool: Check service discovery command
issue_context.body:
<!--

    https://prometheus.io/support-training/

-->
## Proposal

Add a `check sd` command, which takes `--config.file`, the Prometheus configuration file, `--job`, the service discovery job, and `--wait-time`, the time we allow to discover the targets.

```
promtool check sd --config.file=prometheus --job=prometheus --wait-time=5s
```

Discovery would then be performed as normal, relabeling would then be run, and the output would be printed.

(credit to @roidelapluie for the command syntax and the idea to use the existing discovery mechanisms)

**Use case. Why is this important?**

It could be useful for a user to quickly see what any SD is giving them, but especially with the introduction of the HTTP SD they'll be a lot more developers working on SD integrations, and this could make the development process easier.
comments: @roidelapluie in your original proposal for this (https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/8950#discussion_r654402270) you kind of imply machine readable? The current PR from @darshanime has a human readable output, which I think is actually useful... but maybe we should add a `--yaml` flag or such?
I'm trying to debug why some of my job targets aren't found, and this would be an excellent tool to have (the web Service Discovery UI truncates at 100 targets making things difficult).

review_comments: This is looking good, aside from the few comments below. However it needs testing. I think it would make sense that this function takes the place to output to, i.e. `os.Stdout` in normal running. Then write a test that provides its own buffer and at least checks the JSON is valid.
Why can't we use json.Marshall for everything? I would just create a big slice and Marshal it.
